plot: The morning after Mia hears a kitten under the porch, Dad plans to pull up the boards at noon and the only gap is one bean wide; Bup's crust lure gets a paw halfway out and then the crying grows, scared Pim goes in, gets hissed at and runs, Crispy tells him a hiss can just mean 'I'm scared too', and on his second trip Pim finds the twist — the kitten isn't shy, its paw is caught in Grandma's strawberry net lost in a spring storm (mentioned at the start, and Zeek noticed it always cries from the same spot); Pim pushes the loop off a nail, the kitten runs into Mia's arms — then Mom makes it a bed in the bros' own bread basket.

script.title: A Kitten Is Crying Under Our Porch

beats.say: It cried all night! The kitten is still under the porch!
Dad pulls up the porch at noon. Can we save it first?
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
Saturday morning. Warm sun, crunchy leaves, and one tiny cry.
Mia found a grey kitten last night. Thin, scared, and hiding deep.
Mia left a saucer of milk by the steps. Still full.
On the porch, Grandma is grumbling again about her lost strawberry net.
A spring storm blew it away. Nobody ever found it.
Odd. The crying always comes from the exact same spot.
Shy cats hide, Zeek. It comes out when it gets hungry.
Or it is waiting for someone brave enough to go in.
Everyone looks at the porch. Then at the gap in the boards.
The gap is very small. Exactly one bean wide.
No. No, no, no. Kittens chase small, wiggly things!
And I am the smallest, wiggliest thing in this garden!
Pim, it's crying for help. Not for breakfast.
Hold on. Let me try first. Crumbs always work on me.
Bup rolls in a piece of his own crust.
Here, little kitty. It's stale, but it's from the heart.
A tiny grey paw slides out of the dark and reaches.
Then the paw stops. Halfway. And the crying gets louder.
It wants the crumb! So why won't it come and get it?
Same spot. Again. That is not a coincidence.
Ten o'clock. Dad carries a crowbar out of the shed.
Two hours. Then the boards come up, and that kitten panics.
If it panics, it runs deeper. Under the whole house.
Okay. Fine. I'm going in. Somebody hold my bandage.
Holding it. Go, Pim. We're right outside the gap.
Pim squeezes through the boards. Dust. Cobwebs. Old leaves.
It's so dark in here. Something is breathing. Hello?
Two huge green eyes open right in front of him.
The kitten hisses. Pim shoots back out like a cork.
It hissed! It looked right at me and hissed!
Everything hisses at me. Doesn't mean they hate me.
Sometimes it just means, I'm scared too.
Eleven thirty. Dad pulls on his work gloves.
Thirty minutes, Pim! After that it's boards and noise!
Fine. Second time. Shaking twice as much. Going in.
This time, Pim crawls slowly. He hums. The kitten listens.
The kitten pulls toward him. Then it jerks back. And cries.
Wait. Its back paw. There's green string around it!
Green string? Same spot every time? It's not shy. It's stuck!
Green net. Grandma's strawberry net! The storm blew it under here!
The net's loop is caught on an old nail in the boards.
Don't untie it, Pim. Just push the loop off the nail.
Pim pushes with his whole bean body. The loop slides.
Come on, nail! I'm a bean! I'm stronger than I look!
Pop. The loop flies off. The paw is free.
The kitten bolts out of the gap, straight into Mia's arms.
Dad drops the crowbar. Nobody has to pull up anything.
Pim, you went in twice. Twice! I'm so proud I could crumble.
My knees are jelly. Do beans have knees? They're jelly.
That night, Mom makes the kitten a bed. A soft basket.
That basket. That is our basket. That's where we sleep.
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.
